name: cimg
why: A header-only C++ image toolkit; a close call since it is a library, but its image internals are fun to poke.

brief.what_it_is: CImg is a small, open-source C++ library for image processing. You include a single header, CImg.h, in your C++ source and use its classes and methods to load and save many image file formats, read and set pixel values, display, transform and filter images, draw primitives such as text, curves and 3D objects, compute statistics, and handle user interaction on images. Its central type is one image class that holds datasets of up to 4 dimensions, from 1D signals to 3D volumes, with template pixel types such as bool, char, int and float. It also handles image collections and sequences.
brief.why_it_exists: The author, David Tschumperlé, began it in late 1999 during his PhD to help himself and colleagues build image processing algorithms, for data from 2D scalar images up to 3D volumes of diffusion tensors. The README stresses that it is meant to be compact, easy to install and use, multi-platform and generic.
brief.how_it_works: The library is a header-only design: CImg.h is the whole library, and it defines only four classes inside the namespace cimg_library. It builds with a minimal set of standard C++ and system libraries. Optional external libraries such as FFTW3, libpng, libjpeg, libtiff, OpenEXR, OpenCV, OpenMP, ImageMagick and FFmpeg can be plugged in for extra features, and a simple plug-in mechanism lets users extend it.
brief.install_notes: No install or build commands appear in the README or on the homepage. The stated model is to include CImg.h in your own C++ source, and the README says it needs no exotic or complex dependencies. External libraries are optional. The brew formula reports no executables, so this is a library you compile against, not a command-line tool.
brief.standout: It is one header file with four classes and no mandatory dependencies, yet it covers file I/O, drawing, statistics and display, and it supports up to 4D pixel data with templated pixel types. Its dual CeCILL-C / CeCILL licensing and its long history since 1999 also set it apart from newer image libraries.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage says the author is still using, maintaining and updating the library and expects to keep doing so for the next couple of years, and the GitHub README shows a build-and-test CI badge. I found no release date or last-commit date in the pages I read, so I cannot confirm recent activity. The homepage also says it is mainly developed in the author's free time.
brief.caveats: The README gives no build or usage example, so a writer will need the docs or tutorial to show real code. Licensing is CeCILL-C or CeCILL, not MIT or BSD, so check compatibility before commercial use. Because it is a library, not a tool, a general reader may find little to try without writing C++. The homepage's OpenCV link is malformed (http://http://), which is minor. The brew entry has no caveats.
quotes: CImg stands for Cool Image : It is easy to use, efficient and is intended to be a very pleasant toolbox to design image processing algorithms in C++.
It is made of a single header file CImg.h that must be included in your C++ source.
No need for exotic or complex dependencies.
